title: Fail Fast, Fail Loud: Bulletproof Config & Runtime Env Validation with env-schema-guard
excerpt: Stop letting bad configs break production. Learn how env-schema-guard prevents silent container boot crashes, guarantees type coercion, and aggregates errors in under 2.5 KB.
content:
Package 1 • Config Guardian

🛡️ Fail Fast, Fail Loud — Before Production Does

Zero-Dependency Startup Config & Schema Validator for TypeScript & Node.js (< 2.5 KB)

💥 The Silent Production Killer: Bad Configuration

In cloud environments, microservices, and modern web apps, the most frustrating and costly downtime doesn't happen because of algorithmic failure. It happens because of missing or malformed environment variables.

  • If PORT is injected as string "3000a" or "NaN", your server crashes silently after binding.
  • If DATABASE_URL is omitted, your app starts up normally, passes initial health checks, but explodes 10 minutes later when a user attempts checkout.
  • If ENABLE_FEATURE_FLAG is set to "false", naive JavaScript checks like Boolean(process.env.ENABLE_FEATURE_FLAG) evaluate to true because any non-empty string is truthy!

⚡ Why env-schema-guard vs Heavy Alternatives?

🪶

Zero Dependencies

Weighs ~2.5 KB minified. No Zod or Joi dependency tree bloat in your serverless functions or container images.

🔄

Automatic Type Coercion

Converts "8080" to number, "true"/"false" to real boolean, and JSON strings to typed objects seamlessly.

📋

Aggregated Error Diagnostics

Never fix one missing key at a time. Prints every invalid or missing variable in a single, formatted diagnostic report.

💻 Quick Start & Architecture Walkthrough

Define your runtime schema once at startup. TypeScript will automatically infer the full return type:

import { validateEnv } from "env-schema-guard";
import "dotenv/config";

export const env = validateEnv({
  PORT: { 
    type: "port", 
    default: 8080, 
    description: "Web server listening port" 
  },
  NODE_ENV: { 
    type: "string", 
    enum: ["development", "staging", "production"] as const, 
    default: "development" 
  },
  DATABASE_URL: { 
    type: "url", 
    description: "Postgres primary connection pool URL" 
  },
  ENABLE_RATE_LIMIT: { 
    type: "boolean", 
    default: true 
  },
  STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: { 
    type: "string", 
    pattern: /^sk_live_[a-zA-Z0-9]{24,}$/,
    description: "Production Stripe Secret Key" 
  },
  ADMIN_EMAILS: { 
    type: "json", 
    required: false, 
    description: "Array of authorized admin emails" 
  }
});

// Inferred TypeScript types:
// env.PORT -> number
// env.NODE_ENV -> "development" | "staging" | "production"
// env.DATABASE_URL -> string
// env.ENABLE_RATE_LIMIT -> boolean

🏢 Real-World Production Use Cases

1. Docker & Kubernetes Pod Gatekeeper

If Helm charts or ConfigMaps missed a credential, env-schema-guard exits with status code 1 immediately. This stops the unhealthy container before it enters the ingress routing pool.

2. FinTech & Payment Gateway Protection

Strict regex pattern matching ensures developers never accidentally deploy sandbox test keys (sk_test_...) to production financial endpoints.

Free, open source, and MIT licensed. Supports Node.js, Bun, and TypeScript.

title: Retry Smarter, Not Harder: Distributed Systems Resilience with retry-circuit
excerpt: Networks are unreliable. Explore how retry-circuit stops thundering herds with AWS-standard full randomized jitter and halts cascading microservice failures with an integrated 3-state Circuit Breaker.
content:
Package 2 • Resilience Engine

⚡ Retry Smarter, Not Harder

Exponential Backoff, Full Randomized Jitter, & 3-State Circuit Breaker in ~1.5 KB

💥 Your API Isn't Failing — Your Retry Strategy Is

In cloud environments, temporary network glitches, database lock contention, and 429 rate limits are inevitable. But traditional retry loops often make the problem ten times worse:

  • The Thundering Herd Problem: When 1,000 clients fail simultaneously and all retry at the exact same 500ms mark, they DDoS the recovering downstream database into total collapse.
  • Infinite 4xx Retries: Retrying 400 Bad Request or 401 Unauthorized burns server CPU and bandwidth for errors that will never succeed.
  • Cascading Outages: Continuing to spam a service that is completely offline wastes thread pools and exhausts server sockets.

🔄 The 3-State Circuit Breaker Pattern

🟢 CLOSED (Normal)

Requests pass through normally. Failures are tracked. If failures exceed threshold, the circuit trips.

🔴 OPEN (Tripped)

Fails fast immediately without touching the network. Protects down streams from overload.

🟡 HALF-OPEN (Testing)

After cooldown period, allows a single probe request through. If it succeeds, circuit resets to CLOSED.

💻 Production Code Walkthrough

Combining Circuit Breaker, Exponential Backoff, Full Jitter, and Smart Filtering:

import { retrySmart, CircuitBreaker } from "retry-circuit";

// 1. Initialize Circuit Breaker
const paymentBreaker = new CircuitBreaker({
  failureThreshold: 3, // Trip after 3 consecutive failures
  cooldownMs: 15000,   // Wait 15s before probe request
  onStateChange: (state) => console.warn(`[GATEWAY] Circuit changed to: ${state}`)
});

// 2. Wrap critical async operations
export async function executePayment(orderId: string, amount: number) {
  return paymentBreaker.exec(async () => {
    return retrySmart(
      async (attempt) => {
        const res = await fetch("https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges", {
          method: "POST",
          headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
          body: JSON.stringify({ orderId, amount })
        });

        if (!res.ok) {
          const err: any = new Error(`Payment failed: HTTP ${res.status}`);
          err.status = res.status;
          throw err;
        }
        return res.json();
      },
      {
        retries: 4,
        baseDelayMs: 300,
        strategy: "exponential",
        jitter: true, // AWS-standard randomized spread
        timeoutMs: 3000,
        shouldRetry: (err: any) => {
          // Never retry client side errors (400, 401, 404)
          if (err.status >= 400 && err.status < 500 && err.status !== 429) {
            return false;
          }
          return true; // Retry 429 rate-limits, 500, 502, 503
        },
        onRetry: (err, attempt, delay) => {
          console.log(`Retry attempt #${attempt} in ${delay}ms...`);
        }
      }
    );
  });
}

title: Version Your Prompts Like Your Code: Production AI Engineering with prompt-kit-js
excerpt: LLM apps don't fail because of models — they fail because of unversioned prompt chaos. Centralize prompts, enforce strict placeholder safety, and estimate tokens in under 2 KB.
content:
Package 3 • LLM Prompt Manager

🤖 Version Your Prompts Like Your Code

Centralized, Versioned Prompt Registry & Token Estimator for Any LLM (< 2 KB)

💥 The Hidden Chaos of Modern Generative AI Apps

In 90% of AI applications, prompts are written as messy, hardcoded multiline string literals scattered across dozens of controllers. This creates serious production bottlenecks:

  • No Semantic Versioning: When an engineer tweaks prompt wording to fix one edge case, they silently break three other business workflows with zero rollback path.
  • Wasted API Bills: Sending unpopulated templates with missing placeholders like {{user_name}} costs money and returns garbage completions to users.
  • Context Overflow Panics: No pre-flight validation of token length before dispatching requests leads to sudden 400 Bad Request errors.
  • LangChain Bloat: Installing a 100+ MB framework with hundreds of transitive dependencies just for basic string substitution is unacceptable.

✨ Four Core Pillars of prompt-kit-js

🏷️

Semantic Versioning

Register multiple versions (1.0.0, 2.0.0) side-by-side. Pin legacy versions or A/B test variations with ease.

🔒

Strict Variable Safety

Throws MissingVariableError immediately if any required placeholder is missing. Zero wasted LLM API credits.

🧮

Token Estimation

Built-in heuristic tokenizer (~4 chars/token + word weight) provides instant pre-flight checks without multi-megabyte dictionary downloads.

🔌

Provider Agnostic

Works identically with OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Groq, Mistral, Ollama, or local pipelines.

💻 Production Code Walkthrough

Clean, centralized prompt registration and pre-flight token evaluation:

import { PromptRegistry } from "prompt-kit-js";

export const prompts = new PromptRegistry();

// Version 1.0.0
prompts.register({
  id: "code-analyzer",
  version: "1.0.0",
  description: "Standard code reviewer",
  template: "Review the following {{language}} code:
{{code}}",
  variables: ["language", "code"]
});

// Version 2.0.0 (Enhanced with OWASP compliance)
prompts.register({
  id: "code-analyzer",
  version: "2.0.0",
  description: "Senior Security Engineer audit prompt",
  template: `You are a Principal Application Security Engineer.
Audit this {{language}} snippet for CVE vulnerabilities, memory leaks, and injection flaws:

```{{language}}
{{code}}
```

Return JSON: { score: number, issues: string[] }`,
  variables: ["language", "code"],
  tags: ["security", "production", "gpt-4o"]
});

// Render with token pre-flight statistics
const { prompt, estimatedTokens } = prompts.renderWithStats("code-analyzer", {
  language: "TypeScript",
  code: "function computeHash(val) { return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(val).digest('hex'); }"
});

console.log(`Estimated Tokens: ~${estimatedTokens}`);
if (estimatedTokens > 4000) {
  throw new Error("Prompt exceeds single-turn budget!");
}

Free, open source, zero dependencies (< 2 KB). Upgrade your LLMOps pipeline.

npm install prompt-kit-js
